{{ElectionsIL}}
The '''2026 Illinois gubernatorial election''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Illinois]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[JB Pritzker]] is seeking a third term. He is being challenged by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former nominee [[Darren Bailey]].

[[Primary elections]] were held on March 17, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Illinois State Board of Elections |title=Schedule of Future Elections |url=https://www.elections.il.gov/agencyforms/1%20SCHEDULE%20OF%20FUTURE%20ELECTIONS/Schedule%20of%20Elections%20-%20Revised.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260221135507/https://www.elections.il.gov/agencyforms/1%20SCHEDULE%20OF%20FUTURE%20ELECTIONS/Schedule%20of%20Elections%20-%20Revised.pdf |archive-date=February 21, 2026 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=www.elections.il.gov}}</ref> Pritzker secured the Democratic nomination unopposed, while [[Darren Bailey]] secured the Republican nomination with 54% of the vote.<ref>{{cite web |title=Illinois Governor Primary Results 2026 |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-primary-elections/illinois-governor-results |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260411230100/https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-primary-elections/illinois-governor-results |archive-date=April 11, 2026 |access-date=April 19, 2026 |website=[[NBC News]]}}</ref> Pritzker selected [[Christian Mitchell]] as his running mate, as incumbent lieutenant governor [[Julianna Stratton]] is the Democratic nominee for [[2026 United States Senate election in Illinois|U.S. Senate]].

This is the first gubernatorial rematch in Illinois since [[1986 Illinois gubernatorial election|1986]].

== Background ==
A moderately to strongly [[blue state]], Illinois has a reputation for being both the most populous and the most left-leaning state in the Midwest, traits vastly owed to the progressive and diverse [[Chicago metropolitan area]]. Though the state has historically favored Republicans for [[Governor of Illinois|governor]], Democrats have won all but one gubernatorial race in Illinois since [[2002 Illinois gubernatorial election|2002]], the exception being [[Bruce Rauner]]'s narrow victory in [[2014 Illinois gubernatorial election|2014]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Leip |first=David |title=2014 Gubernatorial General Election Results – Illinois |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?year=2014&fips=17&f=0&off=5&elect=0 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250404104935/https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?fips=17&year=2014&f=0&off=5&elect=0 |archive-date=2025-04-04 |access-date=2025-04-09 |website=uselectionatlas.org}}</ref> In addition, Democrats have won Illinois by double-digit margins in every presidential race since [[1992 United States presidential election in Illinois|1992]]; and consistently occupied all of its statewide offices since [[2018 Illinois elections|2019]].  

Incumbent governor [[JB Pritzker]], a member of the Democratic Party, has comfortably won in the past two elections, having first been elected with a 15.6% lead in [[2018 Illinois gubernatorial election|2018]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Leip |first=David |title=2018 Gubernatorial General Election Results – Illinois |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/results/state.php?year=2018&fips=17&f=0&off=5&elect=0 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240520050528/https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?fips=17&year=2018&f=0&off=5&elect=0 |archive-date=2024-05-20 |access-date=2025-04-09 |website=uselectionatlas.org}}</ref> and won re-election by 12.5% in [[2022 Illinois gubernatorial election|2022]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Leip |first=David |title=2022 Gubernatorial General Election Results – Illinois |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/results/state.php?year=2022&fips=17&f=0&off=5&elect=0 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419033643/https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?fips=17&year=2022&f=0&off=5&elect=0 |archive-date=2024-04-19 |access-date=2025-04-09 |website=uselectionatlas.org}}</ref> Despite the state's strong Democratic lean, Republicans are comfortably favored in most of rural Illinois, especially in much of [[Forgottonia|West Central]] and [[Southern Illinois]]. Illinois is one of 16 states that do not have gubernatorial term limits. If Pritzker were to win, he would be the first governor elected to a third term since [[Jim Thompson (Illinois politician)|Jim Thompson]] in [[1982 Illinois gubernatorial election|1982]].
